verdict.rationale: Both changes implement and validate `--percent` the same way and reuse `allocate` and the duplicate check. A enforces 'exactly one of --with/--percent' with argparse's required mutually exclusive group. That is the idiomatic way, keeps the requirement visible in `--help`, and rejects bad usage before any work is done. B hand-rolls the check in `_add` after parsing the amount, which turns a usage error into an application error and hides the requirement from `--help`. B's tests are slightly more thorough (they check nothing is saved and cover the neither case), but that does not outweigh A's cleaner design.
a_issues: No CLI test for giving neither --with nor --percent (argparse handles it, but it is unprotected)
The test rejecting percentages that don't add to 100 does not check that nothing was saved
b_issues: Checks for --with/--percent exclusivity by hand in _add instead of using argparse's mutually exclusive group; --help no longer shows that one of them is required
Runs the exclusivity check after parse_amount, so a bad amount combined with bad options reports the amount error first
parse_percent does not strip whitespace around the number, so 'alice= 50' is rejected
Parametrized rejection test does not match on the error message, so it would pass for the wrong reason
